claim: The asset update DTO now accepts rating: -1 but BaseSearchSchema.rating in search.dto.ts still carries .min(1).max(5), so /search/metadata, /search/smart, /search/random and /search/statistics return 400 when filtering for rating -1; the search x-immich-history entry 'Using -1 as a rating is no longer valid' is also now false. Verified: UPDATE rating=-1 accepted, SEARCH rating=-1 rejected.
raw: #1 🟠 High: Write path re-permits `rating: -1` but the search filter still rejects it

claim: Replacing .min(1).max(5) with a .refine() drops the rating bounds from the generated OpenAPI spec: UpdateAssetDto and AssetBulkUpdateDto rating now publish minimum -9007199254740991 / maximum 9007199254740991 next to a description saying range [1-5], so spec-validating consumers accept 0, 6, -50 as contract-valid. Occurrence count of the literal went 228 -> 232, exactly the two rating fields touched. Suggested fix: z.union([z.literal(-1), z.int().min(1).max(5)]).
raw: #2 🟠 High: The `.refine()` rewrite drops the rating range constraint from the generated OpenAPI contract

claim: metadata.service.ts:308 still clamps with validateRange(exifTags.Rating, 1, 5) (was -1,5 before 99281de). A user-set rating -1 is written to the XMP sidecar by SidecarWrite, which then unlocks 'rating'; the next metadata extraction (REFRESH_METADATA / library rescan) reads -1 back, clamps it to null, and the upsert with lockedPropertiesBehavior 'skip' overwrites the stored -1 with null, silently erasing the rejected mark. The deleted 'should handle valid negative rating value' spec case is also not restored.
raw: #3 🟠 High: A user-set `rating: -1` is silently erased by the next metadata extraction

claim: No test asserts that rating: -1 is accepted: the change updates the two rejection cases (7, -2) but does not restore { rating: -1 } to the 'should leave correct ratings as-is' array that 99281de removed, and no test anywhere in the repo sends -1 as an accepted value. Probe: with 'v === -1 ||' removed from the refine predicate the spec still reports 42 passed. e2e and metadata.service.spec -1 coverage deleted by 99281de is also not restored.
raw: #4 🟠 High: No test asserts that `rating: -1` is accepted — the sole behavior this change adds

claim: ExifResponseSchema.rating still uses z.int().min(1).max(5).nullish().default(null), so after PUT /assets/:id {rating:-1} succeeds, GET /assets/:id returns exifInfo.rating: -1 which the published ExifResponseDto schema declares invalid (minimum 1). No runtime 500 because no controller applies @ZodSerializerDto; contract-level defect. Verified: ExifResponseSchema.safeParse({ rating: -1 }) fails.
raw: M1 — server/src/dtos/exif.dto.ts:32 — response schema still forbids the value the request schema now accepts.

claim: Deleting the already-applied migration 1780592070031-ConvertNegativeRatingToNull.ts will hard-fail server startup for any database that ran it: Kysely's Migrator #ensureNoMissingMigrations runs unconditionally and throws 'corrupted migrations: previously executed migration <name> is missing', which runMigrations() rethrows, with no allowlist/baseline bypass. The migration sat on mainline ~3 days; whether it reached a released or nightly build could not be established (no git tags). Fix would be to keep the file with a no-op up().
raw: M2 — server/src/schema/migrations/1780592070031-ConvertNegativeRatingToNull.ts (deleted) — deleting an already-applied migration will hard-fail server startup for any database that ran it.
